clauses.reason: This clause is the whole operative paragraph of Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979: by the authority of the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, Executive Order No. 12140 is, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The act is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28. The deleted sentence was the sunset of EO 12140 (midnight on September 30, 1979), so the order took effect before that sunset could run. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986) later orders that the Executive Orders it lists, and their amendments ("any amendments thereto, are revoked:"), are revoked, and its table includes 12162; the held text states no effective date later than signing and no exception, so that revocation operated from 1986-02-25. It is a later event, not the first end of this clause, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation for a command already performed. The surviving effect of the amendment is described in the savings statement.

research_rationale:
EO 12162 (signed 1979-09-28, 44 FR 56665, Federal Register of October 2, 1979) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12162.txt, registered as ORIGINAL:EO:12162). Identity: the heading names Executive Order 12162 of September 28, 1979, titled Amendment to Executive Order 12140, signed at The White House on September 28, 1979. The order is a single operative paragraph: acting under the Constitution, the statutes and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, it amends Executive Order No. 12140, in the words of the held text, "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." The held text of EO 12140 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12140.txt, 44 FR 31159) shows that first sentence provided that the order terminates, unless extended, at midnight on September 30, 1979 (paraphrased, not quoted), so the amendment removed 12140's own sunset two days before it would have run; the second sentence (the Secretary of Energy may revoke the delegation) was left in place. The amendment is performed in the present tense by the order itself, so the clause was executed and exhausted when the order was signed on 1979-09-28; the consequence (EO 12140 no longer terminating on 1979-09-30) is a surviving effect recorded in the savings statement, not a continuing command of EO 12162. The later express revocation by EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; 51 FR 7237) is recorded as a later event and is not the first end, because a later revocation does not prove first cessation of a command already performed (owner ruling 2026-10-28, points 1 and 3). The dossier question 'target provision not located: EO:12553' is answered: the held text of EO 12553 lists 12162 in its table of revoked orders. Own-terms: no sunset, condition or duration in the order. The packet's machine searches (current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr, no hits for this order; later-events:ofr_catalog, two leads, both the EO 12553 note 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986') were read with their coverage notes and surfaced no earlier instrument. The only other held-text citation of the number, FRDOC 97-2965, mentions "Executive Order 12162, Federalism, dated October 26, 1987", which is not this order (a different order number and subject) and is not a later event.

savings.reason: The amendment made by EO 12162 on 1979-09-28 is an accrued effect: EO 12140 was not terminated by its own first-sentence sunset on 1979-09-30 and continued as amended until it ended by some later act. EO 12553 revokes the Executive Orders it lists together with their amendments, and its table lists both 12140 and 12162; the held text of EO 12553 contains no exception, saving or pending-matter provision for either. The date and cause of the end of EO 12140 itself (the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act authority it rests on, or the 1986 revocation) is not established by a held source in this packet and is not asserted; it is the subject of EO 12140's own lifecycle, not of EO 12162's executed amendment.
